name: Lampung
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_quote: Words, both derived and underived, are stressed on the final syllable. This word stress, however, is very slight and it is often skewed by the position of the word in the intonation contour. (Walker 1975:5)

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: the primary source the whole chain rests on (Walker 1976 NUSA 2) is although the record still says 'not held by the project'; I opened p.15 (= p.5, sec. 2.41) and the StressTyp2 passage is there with one trivial word variant ('non-derived' vs 'underived'); the K&H secondary sentence is also confirmed in a held text. (2) Deciding source: a 49-pp 1976 structuralist grammar sketch (condensed 1973 Cornell dissertation), impressionistic, but it is Glottolog's only 'grammar' for lamp1243 and the source StressTyp2, WALS and Kaufman & Himmelmann all cite; Crossref/Semantic Scholar empty; K&H 2019 still cite only Walker). Languoid identity is fine: Way Lima Pesisir = Lampung Api = lamp1243. (3) Coding: 'fixed final' matches Walker's explicit word-stress statemen
audit.second_reader_evidence: Independent re-check of the held primary and of the compilers reading; all three of its page claims verified against fresh 150-dpi renders of the scan we hold (SEAlang open scan, no text; PDF page = grammar page + 10).
